Help clients show where they hurt using familiar body areas and a visual map, while preserving the consultation form.
Iteration 1 goal
Build a reliable, testable body map. Let clients select an area and see the 3D model focus there. Investigate submission and deployment blockers.

slides.title: Design decisions
slides.text:
Design decisions
Familiar areas: expanded to twelve regions, including Arm and Leg
Visual interaction: use the 3D map instead of asking for anatomical terms; exact spot remains optional
Stable architecture: separate model catalog, area mappings, focus rules and selection state
Reproducible testing: vendor model data locally and run browser tests in CI

brief.goal: Get approval for a one-month pilot
brief.keyMessage: Start small and learn before we amplify

slides.title: A quieter way to launch
slides.text:
A quieter way to launch
Start small, learn quickly, scale when the signal is clear.
Northwind Labs | Q3 planning

slides.title: Clarity is already compounding
slides.text:
Clarity is already compounding
Activation rose from 61% to 74% in six weeks.
The first ten minutes got easier.
Week 1: 61% · Week 3: 68% · Week 6: 74%

slides.title: Three deliberate moves
slides.text:
Three deliberate moves
Invite the users who feel the problem most sharply.
Give them a guided first week.
Let what we learn shape the public story.

slides.title: What we will watch
slides.text:
What we will watch
Week-one activation, target 80%
Support tickets per new account
Share of invited users who invite a teammate

slides.title: What could go wrong
slides.text:
What could go wrong
A small cohort may not represent everyone.
The guided week needs two people from support.
Competitors may launch louder first.

slides.title: The ask
slides.text:
The ask
One focused month.
One shared measure of success.
Permission to learn before we amplify.

brief.goal: Help first-year students understand how photosynthesis turns light into stored energy
brief.keyMessage: Light reactions capture energy; the Calvin cycle stores it in sugar

slides.title: Photosynthesis
slides.text:
Photosynthesis
How plants turn light into food
BIO 101 · Week 4

slides.title: The overall equation
slides.text:
The overall equation
6 CO2 + 6 H2O + light → C6H12O6 + 6 O2
Inputs: carbon dioxide, water, light
Outputs: glucose, oxygen

slides.title: Where it happens
slides.text:
Where it happens
Chloroplasts
Thylakoid membranes: light reactions
Stroma: Calvin cycle

slides.title: Light reactions
slides.text:
Light reactions
Chlorophyll absorbs light
Water is split, releasing O2
Energy is stored in ATP and NADPH

slides.title: The Calvin cycle
slides.text:
The Calvin cycle
Uses ATP and NADPH
Fixes CO2 into sugar
RuBisCO is the key enzyme
3 turns → 1 G3P molecule

slides.title: Why it matters
slides.text:
Why it matters
Nearly all food chains start here
Produces the oxygen we breathe
Removes CO2 from the atmosphere
Question for next week: what limits the rate?
